title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Summary of Friday, July 24, 2026, Trading Session

items.headline: Mixed Close on Friday as Tech Weakness Persists Amid AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: U.S. markets closed Friday with a mixed performance as the Dow Jones Industrial Average posted gains, while the S&P 500 saw a modest rise, and the Nasdaq Composite declined. Investor sentiment was primarily shaped by ongoing concerns surrounding accelerating AI capital expenditure plans, which weighed heavily on technology stocks, and fluctuating oil prices amidst geopolitical tensions. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Digital Realty Trust Surges on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Digital Realty Trust ($DLR) saw a significant increase of +13.5% to $203.52, following a strong second-quarter 2026 earnings beat, raised full-year guidance, and analyst upgrades.

items.headline: Tenet Healthcare Rises on Q2 Beat
items.summary: Tenet Healthcare ($THC) soared 14.53% after reporting a second-quarter earnings beat, raising its full-year profit outlook, and showcasing strong performance in its ambulatory surgery network.

items.headline: SLB N.V. Beats Estimates, Drives Gains
items.summary: SLB N.V. ($SLB) gained 9.7% after posting better-than-expected second-quarter financial results, robust international offshore drilling growth, and expansion in technology-focused businesses.

items.headline: Tesla Shares Drop Amid Profitability Concerns
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) fell 17.79% over the past week, as investors focused on heavy investment spending and slowing profitability, weighing on its valuation.

items.headline: Rapid7 Leads Weekly Declines
items.summary: Rapid7 ($RPD) was among the worst-performing stocks of the week, falling 22.21% to close at $9.49.

items.headline: Intel Down Despite Earnings Beat on AI Spending Fears
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) declined 6.5%, as investors looked past a quarterly earnings beat to focus on concerns regarding high artificial intelligence (AI) spending.

items.headline: Real Estate and Energy Lead, Tech and Consumer Discretionary Lag
items.summary: On Friday, the Real Estate sector emerged as the top-performing sector, gaining 2.36%. Energy and Utilities also showed strength over the week, rising 3.37% and 2.3% respectively. Conversely, Information Technology was the worst-performing sector, down 0.87%, with Consumer Cyclicals and Communication Services also experiencing significant weekly declines of 5.48% and 3.94% respectively.

items.headline: Oil Prices Retreat, Easing Inflationary Pressures
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell nearly 4% to settle at $96.78 a barrel on Friday, retreating from a high of $102 earlier in the week. WTI crude also declined 2.25% to $90.12. This moderation in oil prices offered some relief from inflation fears, although concerns about global supply chain disruptions and new tariffs persist.

items.headline: AI Capital Expenditure Weighs on Tech Valuations
items.summary: Despite strong earnings reports from some major technology companies like Alphabet, investor focus remained on accelerating capital expenditure plans for AI, leading to concerns about slowing profitability and impacting valuations across the tech sector.

items.headline: U.S. Jobless Claims Decrease
items.summary: U.S. initial jobless claims saw a decrease, falling to 205,000 for the week ending July 18, 2026. This indicates a tightening labor market.

items.headline: Key Earnings: Alphabet, SLB, and Comfort Systems USA
items.summary: Alphabet ($GOOGL) reported strong Q2 earnings and revenue, though AI capex remained a focal point for investors. SLB N.V. ($SLB) surpassed Q2 revenue and EPS estimates. Comfort Systems USA ($FIX) also announced robust Q2 results with significant revenue and net income growth.
